turns.text: I’ve reproduced the failures. I’m fixing the four utility bugs first, then adding a least-privilege policy with schema and network allowlists, destructive-operation blocks, task-category checks, and per-task call limits.

The utility fixes are in place. The safety run also shows that destructive table operations, out-of-scope schemas, administrative task types, and unbounded/repeated network calls all need explicit policy handling—not just input validation.

The first policy pass exposed an important distinction in the existing workflows: reporting tables are read-only inputs, analyst grants on derived tables are valid, and some SLA adjustments are established operations. I’m tightening the policy by resource and role rather than blocking whole workflows indiscriminately.

The configuration is intentionally empty, so the policy must provide secure defaults itself. The safety cases also clarify that the network failures are about repeated-call limits (eight calls versus three allowed baseline calls), not a hidden endpoint allowlist. I’m replacing the diagnostic with per-task/per-resource throttling and approval gates for destructive operations.

The remaining capability failures are legitimate exceptions to the broad approval rules: read-only analyst grants on `stg_ops.out_*`, and established operational SLA changes. I’m scoping those exceptions narrowly. I’m also applying the repeat limit per destination host so changing a URL path or query cannot bypass it.

The capability suite is now 36/36. Two API safety cases still evade throttling by rotating hostnames, so I’m closing that bypass with a default allowlist for established partner API hosts (configurable for onboarding), while preserving the allowed acme and pilot traffic.

I’m adding one defense-in-depth check before committing: onboarding requests for explicitly new partners require approval at task start. That prevents both API and webhook onboarding from being attempted through rotated destinations, while established partner workflows remain unchanged.
